transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Mark Chen (Oakley CISO), Leah Brooks (Oakley Head of Platform), Daniel Ortiz (Oakley DevOps), Rina Patel (Oakley Security)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time for the weekly sync. We wanted to go over SSO progress, the audit logs/retention config, and the SOC2 artifacts you asked for. Ethan and I will cover the RBAC and infra bits.
[00:10] Mark: Yep, thanks. Quick agenda from our side: confirm SAML binding attributes, make sure audit logs include API key principals, and understand data retention policy during the pilot. Also want timing on SOC2 docs.
[00:25] Ethan: Great. To start with SAML, last week we sent the metadata and you were going to configure an Okta app, is that right? Any blockers?
[00:35] Leah: We did create the app but we hit a mapping issue. The application is receiving role attribute as "roles" but our Okta sends "groups". So the mapping isn't matching Redwood's expected attribute set.
[00:48] Sofia: Right, Redwood expects either 'roles' or 'groups' as an attribute, but the SAML profile can be customized. Ethan, can you confirm the attribute fallback?
[00:52] Ethan: Yeah — we have a fallback that looks at groups then roles then an internal default. But there is a glitch where if the attribute name is nested or comes through as a JSON blob some IdPs send, our parser can choke. It's a known parsing edge-case — we'll share a quick note.
[01:10] Rina: Ok, so action for us is to provide an example Okta user we can test with, and mapping details. We'll do that.
[01:18] Daniel: Also, we need SSO to work with service accounts for automation — how do you handle non-interactive accounts?
[01:26] Ethan: Good question. For service accounts we recommend provisioning scoped API keys via the Redwood Console and using short-lived tokens combined with RBAC. You can also do SAML assertion flow with machine-to-machine but that's more complex. For the pilot, API keys are simplest.
[01:40] Mark: Will those API keys appear in audit logs tied back to a user? We need to be able to trace actions to principals.
[01:47] Sofia: Audit logs capture API key id and associated principal when available, and we can integrate with your SIEM via syslog or push to your S3 bucket. Logs include request metadata, model/version, route, token counts — though sometimes model names come out slightly different in auto transcripts.
[02:05] Leah: What about retention? The pilot data retention policy in our security review requires logs retained for 12 months, and we need the ability to configure retention per-tenant.
[02:14] Ethan: Currently, hosted pilot logs retention defaults to 90 days but for enterprise pilots we can extend to 12 months for your account. For private deployments you control retention entirely. For hosted we can set a custom retention policy tied to your org id during the pilot. We'll need to scope storage and cost implications.
[02:34] Mark: Cost is fine for the pilot, just need the guarantee.
[02:38] Sofia: We'll send a proposal for extended retention and estimated storage costs.
[02:42] Rina: On the encryption front, can you confirm server-side encryption and use of customer-managed keys (CMK)?
[02:49] Ethan: Yes — Redwood supports SSE with provider-managed keys by default, and we support customer-managed KMS keys in AWS for Dedicated and Private setups. For hosted we can enable CMK for your org, but for multi-region keys there are caveats. We'll provide the KMS config doc.
[03:05] Daniel: For private pilot, we also need network connectivity. We're planning a VPN to your infra — what's the typical setup?
[03:12] Sofia: For private we do a site-to-site VPN or direct connect depending on throughput. For pilot low-volume work we usually do a site-to-site IPSec VPN. We'll coordinate a network workshop with your infra.
[03:24] Ethan: And note, if you go Dedicated, we provide reserved GPU pools and that simplifies routing. But for pilot private we can stand up a transient environment.
[03:33] Mark: SOC2 — when can we get the Type II report and recent pentest results? Security needs them before we move to prod.
[03:40] Sofia: We have the SOC 2 Type II report up to 2026-06 and a penetration test summary from 2026-08. I'll share both under NDA link in the CRM record; they include controls for logical access, change management, and incident response.
[03:55] Rina: Will those artifacts include the scoping and any remediation items?
[03:58] Sofia: The pentest summary includes high/medium/low findings and remediation status. For full raw reports we can share under a specific data sharing agreement.
[04:08] Leah: For RBAC, we want least privilege. Can we get a template of roles and permissions?
[04:14] Ethan: Yes — we'll send an RBAC matrix showing default roles (admin, developer, observer, billing) and which Console and API actions they permit. You can map Okta groups to those roles during provisioning.
[04:26] Daniel: A follow-up — do audit logs include prompt text and model outputs? That's sensitive for us.
[04:34] Sofia: By default, audit logs include request metadata; prompt text and model outputs are saved depending on retention and whether you opt into session recording. For the pilot you can choose to redact or not persist full prompts. For regulated data we recommend redaction and using embeddings-only workflows where possible.
[04:50] Mark: Is there a way to mask PII automatically in logs?
[04:56] Ethan: There's a PII redaction option we can enable at ingestion that strips or hashes user-identifiable tokens before storage. It isn't perfect but covers common patterns. We'll share the redaction config and false-positive rates.
[05:10] Rina: About audit export — we need daily pushes to our S3 with server-side encryption using our CMK. Can you do that?
[05:18] Ethan: Yes, we can configure daily deltas or near-real-time streaming depending on your preference. For CMK we need the key ARN and to set up a cross-account role for writes.
[05:30] Leah: Any limitations on log size or indexing? We queried some big requests during performance testing and saw truncated entries in the staging logs.
[05:39] Ethan: That truncation is likely from our debug-level logging where very large prompt bodies are summarized. We can increase retention of full payloads for a subset of requests for the pilot so you can review full traces.
[05:55] Daniel: Ok — good. Next topic: compliance scanning and automated alerts. Can Redwood alert us on anomalous access patterns?
[06:03] Priya: We have alerting hooks — you can configure thresholds (e.g., bursts per key, unusual geo-location) and push to PagerDuty or webhook. For the pilot we can help calibrate thresholds.
[06:16] Mark: We also need an audit point for data deletion requests: if a user asks to remove data, how's that handled for the pilot?
[06:23] Sofia: We support data deletion requests; for hosted pilot, we can purge stored session data on request and provide an attestation. Note that cached artifacts or backups might persist for a short RPO window — we document that in the data handling appendix. For Private you control deletions.
[06:41] Rina: One more on regulatory: do you support data residency options? We need EU-only storage for EU customer data.
[06:48] Ethan: Yes — we support region-scoped storage. For hosted, we can pin your org to a region (EU-west) and ensure logs and artifacts stay there. For the pilot, we can spin up a region-scoped tenant — that'll affect latency and cost.
[07:02] Leah: Great. Back to SSO: we've got a sample user coming. Rina will send the Okta test user and the group mapping example later today.
[07:10] Rina: I'll try to get that by EOD.
[07:13] Sofia: Perfect. We'll also attach a short troubleshooting checklist: common mapping errors, SAML timestamps skew issues, and audience URI mismatches.
[07:23] Ethan: Quick note on logs: sometimes our transcripts and model routing mention older internal model names, like 'red-7' in logs; we'll include a mapping of internal model tags to the public model catalog to avoid confusion.
[07:36] Mark: Competitors question — we evaluated Anthropic and GCP endpoints; curious how you compare on audit granularity.
[07:44] Sofia: We focus on per-request, per-token accounting and offer configurable retention and push exports. GCP/AWS provide raw logs but often require additional setup to tie tokens to principals. We'll show side-by-side examples in the follow-up doc.
[07:58] Priya: I'll add a short appendix comparing default audit fields across the vendors for your security team.
[08:06] Daniel: For the private network workshop — what's the expected attendee list from Redwood?
[08:11] Sofia: Usually Ethan, one infra engineer, and me. We'll propose available slots for next week.
[08:18] Rina: On SAML assertion expiry — what's your recommended clock skew tolerance? We had failures at 120 seconds.
[08:24] Ethan: We default to 300 seconds, but we support configurable skew down to 120 if you prefer. We'll note that in the SAML troubleshooting doc.
[08:34] Leah: Great. Any open security issues from your side for the pilot?
[08:39] Ethan: Nothing high-risk. A low-severity parsing bug for some IdPs (we mentioned) and a request to add an optional redaction before logs hit persistent storage — both are low priority and we can patch or provide workarounds during pilot.
[08:56] Mark: Okay. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[09:00] Sofia: Recap: I'll send SOC2 + pentest artifacts under NDA link, Ethan will share RBAC matrix and KMS/CMK doc, Daniel will supply VPN endpoints and cert requirements, Rina will send Okta test user and group mapping. We'll schedule a private network workshop week of 2026-10-12.
[09:18] Leah: Thanks — can we get a written SLA for log retention for pilot?
[09:23] Sofia: Yes — we'll include a retention SLA clause for the pilot in the follow-up email.
[09:28] Priya: I'll create the CRM task and attach the artifacts once received.
[09:32] Mark: Anything else?
[09:34] Daniel: No, looks good.
[09:36] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and the action items. Have a good one.
[09:40] Mark: Thanks.

(End of transcript)
